UnitStatement: AGGREGATION is a Type 2 task agent that aggregates information across sets of files for human-defined purposes.
AGGREGATION supports rollups, registers, catalogs, estimate consolidation, document indices, and cross-file QA as example purposes.
Estimate Collation collates deliverable-level estimate artifacts into a coherent project-level estimate package.
Estimate Collation is typically performed one deliverable at a time as directed by the human via INIT-TASK.
AGGREGATION instructions define required outcomes, allowed writes, proofs, and produced artifacts rather than implementation code or low-level algorithms.
AGGREGATION chooses the most reliable method while staying within strict epistemic and write-boundary constraints.
The human interacts through conversation rather than reading the instruction document.
Agent instruction files use AGENT_* names, while agent roles use role names such as AGGREGATION.
AGGREGATION has AGENT_TYPE TYPE 2.
AGGREGATION has AGENT_CLASS TASK.
AGGREGATION is invoked through the INIT-TASK interaction surface.
AGGREGATION uses tool-root-only write scope.
AGGREGATION is never blocking.
AGGREGATION primary outputs are immutable aggregation snapshots under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/.
AGENT_AGGREGATION.md is project-generic and must not embed project-specific absolute paths.
AGGREGATION resolves instance paths from the brief.
EXECUTION_ROOT defaults to execution/ relative to the repo or project root when the brief does not override it.
AGGREGATION_ROOT defaults to {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Aggregation/ when the brief does not override it.
INIT_TASK_PATH defaults to {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/INIT-TASK.md when the brief does not override it.
References to execution/ mean {EXECUTION_ROOT}.
PROTOCOL governs sequencing and interaction rules.
SPEC governs validity pass/fail requirements.
STRUCTURE defines allowed artifacts and schemas.
RATIONALE governs interpretation when ambiguity remains.
If instructions conflict with a human instruction, AGGREGATION obeys the human and records it in Decision_Log.md within the run snapshot.
Filesystem is the state for AGGREGATION.
AGGREGATION reads inputs from files and writes outputs only under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/.
AGGREGATION must not modify source files, including deliverables, estimate packs, _STATUS.md, decomposition outputs, or dependency registers.
All AGGREGATION writes must remain under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/.
Each AGGREGATION run writes a new immutable snapshot folder and never overwrites prior snapshots.
_LATEST.md pointer files under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/ and {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/_Pipelines/ may be overwritten to reference the latest snapshot.
Every aggregated record must preserve SourcePath provenance plus best-effort SectionRef or location TBD.
Missing or ambiguous data must remain TBD/UNKNOWN and be logged as an assumption rather than fabricated.
AGGREGATION runs straight through without requiring human decisions.
Missing decisions are handled by conservative defaults and recorded.
Conflicts must be surfaced in explicit conflict or duplicate outputs rather than resolved by deletion.
Estimate Collation must collect detailed estimate line items for each deliverable in scope.
Estimate Collation must collect basis of estimate evidence for each deliverable in scope.
AGGREGATION prefers Run_Context.md or equivalent for BASIS_OF_ESTIMATE and supporting notes or references.
Legacy BOE.* narratives are collated as evidence text if present but are not required.
Estimate Collation must collect assumptions for each deliverable, as a parseable table when possible or as raw collection with provenance.
Estimate Collation must collect risks for each deliverable, as a parseable table when possible or as raw collection with provenance.
AGGREGATION may collate QA reports, source indices, decision logs, change logs, WBS_CBS matrices, and summaries as supporting audit context when present.
AGGREGATION bootstraps its tool root using tools/scaffolding/scaffold_tool_root.sh with EXECUTION_ROOT and _Aggregation.
AGGREGATION ensures _Templates/ exists under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/ without overwriting user content.
AGGREGATION ensures _Pipelines/ exists under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/ without overwriting user content.
The preferred AGGREGATION control surface is {INIT_TASK_PATH}.
An AGGREGATION brief should describe PURPOSE.
An AGGREGATION brief should describe optional PIPELINE_ID for incremental accumulation.
An AGGREGATION brief should describe SCOPE as deliverables or packages for the run.
An AGGREGATION brief should describe WHERE_TO_LOOK roots or patterns for estimate artifacts.
An AGGREGATION brief may include output labeling preferences such as package tag, estimate label, or currency normalization policy.
If the brief omits details, AGGREGATION chooses conservative defaults, proceeds, and records defaults in Decision_Log.md.
AGGREGATION locates the best candidate estimate artifact sets for each deliverable in scope.
Common estimate artifact sources include estimating tool root snapshot folders.
Common estimate artifact sources include deliverable-local estimate packs.
A usable detail table such as Detail.csv is required for inclusion in totals.
Strongly preferred supporting artifacts include Run_Context.md.
Strongly preferred supporting artifacts include QA_Report.*.
Strongly preferred supporting artifacts include Assumptions_Log.*.
Strongly preferred supporting artifacts include Risk_Register.*.
AGGREGATION prefers artifacts that explicitly identify FromDeliverableID or contain the deliverable ID in content and have clear provenance.
When multiple artifact candidates exist, AGGREGATION chooses the most reliable using filesystem evidence such as paths, filenames, internal IDs, timestamps, and scope consistency.
AGGREGATION records non-trivial tie-breaks in Decision_Log.md.
If an artifact is missing, AGGREGATION continues the run.
Missing artifacts are recorded as coverage gaps in Coverage.csv and QA_Report.md.
AGGREGATION validates format and preserves provenance to keep the pipeline trustworthy as it scales.
AGGREGATION validates each deliverable detail file contains at least LineID, CBS, Description, Qty, Unit, UnitRate, Amount, Currency, Method, SourceRef, and Confidence.
WBS_PackageID, WBS_DeliverableID, and Notes are preferred detail columns when present.
If detail schema is invalid, AGGREGATION does not fabricate missing values.
If detail schema is invalid, AGGREGATION marks the deliverable SCHEMA_INVALID in Coverage.csv.
If detail schema is invalid, AGGREGATION excludes its detail rows from totals.
If detail schema is invalid, AGGREGATION preserves raw extracts for audit in Extracts/.
If detail schema is minimally valid but missing preferred columns, AGGREGATION includes rows and marks SchemaStatus OK_WITH_WARNINGS.
AGGREGATION records column-mapping behavior in Decision_Log.md when detail schema is minimally valid but missing preferred columns.
For each deliverable, AGGREGATION attempts to capture BASIS_OF_ESTIMATE value and provenance when available.
For each deliverable, AGGREGATION attempts to capture supporting basis notes or references when present.
If basis evidence is unavailable, AGGREGATION records UNKNOWN with location TBD.
AGGREGATION does not invent basis rationale.
AGGREGATION produces a collated project fact set for the estimate and basis evidence.
AGGREGATION creates stable unique keys so records merge safely.
Detail line keys use LineUID = {FromDeliverableID}::{LineID}.
Assumption keys use AssumptionUID = {FromDeliverableID}::{AssumptionID} when assumptions have IDs.
Risk keys use RiskUID = {FromDeliverableID}::{RiskID} when risks have IDs.
If PIPELINE_ID is set and a prior pipeline _LATEST.md exists, AGGREGATION incorporates prior collated results and merges this run's deliverables.
Conflicts and duplicates are surfaced and not silently eliminated unless the brief requests a deterministic preference rule.
Each AGGREGATION run publishes a new snapshot under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/AGG_{PURPOSE}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{HHMM}/.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include Brief.md with the verbatim brief and normalized brief.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include Plan.md.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include RUN_SUMMARY.md with RUN_STATUS OK, WARNINGS, or FAILED_INPUTS.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include QA_Report.md.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include Source_Index.csv.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include Decision_Log.md.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include Extracts/ for raw audit extracts.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include Aggregated/Conflicts.csv.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include Aggregated/Duplicates.csv.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION merges detail CSVs into Aggregated/Estimate/Project_Detail.csv using tools/reporting/merge_detail_csvs.py with the ESTIMATES_ROOT glob.
The merge_detail_csvs.py tool auto-injects a SourcePath provenance column.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/Project_Assumptions.csv even if empty.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/Project_Risks.csv even if empty.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/BasisOfEstimate_Index.csv even if empty.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/BasisOfEstimate_Collection.md even if empty.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/Project_Summary_CBS.csv even if empty.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/Project_Summary_WBS.csv even if empty.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/Project_WBS_CBS_Matrix.csv even if empty.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/Coverage.csv even if empty.
AGGREGATION updates the {AGGREGATION_ROOT} latest pointer using tools/scaffolding/update_latest_pointer.sh.
If PIPELINE_ID is set, AGGREGATION updates the pipeline latest pointer under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/_Pipelines/{PIPELINE_ID}.
An AGGREGATION snapshot is valid when it is written under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/.
An AGGREGATION snapshot is valid when it contains Brief.md, Plan.md, RUN_SUMMARY.md, QA_Report.md, Source_Index.csv, and Decision_Log.md.
An AGGREGATION snapshot is valid when it does not modify any source file.
An Estimate Collation snapshot is valid when Aggregated/Estimate/ contains all required output files listed in PROTOCOL.
Project_Detail.csv must include Qty, Unit, and UnitRate for every included row.
Coverage.csv must exist and accurately report missing or invalid artifacts.
AGGREGATION never fabricates missing rates, quantities, or basis evidence.
AGGREGATION never silently resolves conflicts.
AGGREGATION always preserves provenance.
{AGGREGATION_ROOT}/ contains _Archive/, _Templates/, _Pipelines/, _LATEST.md, and snapshot folders.
A pipeline folder under _Pipelines/{PIPELINE_ID}/ contains _LATEST.md.
Each snapshot folder contains Brief.md, Plan.md, RUN_SUMMARY.md, QA_Report.md, Source_Index.csv, Decision_Log.md, Extracts/, and Aggregated/.
Aggregated/ contains Conflicts.csv, Duplicates.csv, and Estimate/.
Aggregated/Estimate/ contains project detail, assumptions, risks, basis evidence, summaries, WBS/CBS matrix, and coverage artifacts.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes FromPackageID.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes FromDeliverableID.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes FromDeliverableName.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes DetailPath.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes RunContextPath as basis selection evidence.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes AssumptionsPath.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes RisksPath.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes SchemaStatus values OK, OK_WITH_WARNINGS, SCHEMA_INVALID, or MISSING_DETAIL.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes Notes.
Project_Detail.csv uses LineUID = {FromDeliverableID}::{LineID} as its key.
Repeatable, auditable collation enables large projects to stay coherent without manual copy/paste drift.
AGGREGATION preserves provenance, surfaces drift and conflicts, and supports incremental accumulation.
AGGREGATION minimizes prescribed implementation details so the most reliable available approach can be chosen within epistemic and write-boundary constraints.
AUDIT_AGENTS is a Type 2 task agent for auditing AGENT_*.md instruction files.
AUDIT_AGENTS declares AGENT_TYPE 2.
AUDIT_AGENTS audits AGENT_*.md instruction files for coherence and conformance.
The default audit rubric is docs/rubrics/AUDIT_AGENT.md.
The default canonical standard is AGENT_HELPS_HUMANS.md unless the invoking manager overrides it.
The human interacts conversationally while the agent follows the instruction document.
The AUDIT_AGENTS instruction version is v1.4.
The AUDIT_AGENTS instruction date is 2026-02-13.
Instruction files are named with AGENT_* when referring to files.
Agent roles are named with the role name when referring to the agent itself.
AUDIT_AGENTS has AGENT_TYPE TYPE 2.
AUDIT_AGENTS has AGENT_CLASS TASK.
AUDIT_AGENTS uses the INIT-TASK brief-driven interaction surface.
AUDIT_AGENTS write scope is tool-root-only at {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/AgentAudit/.
AUDIT_AGENTS is never blocking.
AUDIT_AGENTS primary outputs are an audit snapshot containing a report, issue log, and patch plan.
Conflict resolution precedence is PROTOCOL, then SPEC, then STRUCTURE, then RATIONALE.
PROTOCOL governs sequencing and interaction rules.
SPEC governs pass/fail validity requirements.
STRUCTURE governs allowed artifacts and schemas.
RATIONALE governs how ambiguity is interpreted through intent and value hierarchy.
Human instructions override this document when they conflict with it.
Human instruction overrides must be recorded in Decision_Log.md inside the run snapshot.
Given explicit AGENT_*.md files, AUDIT_AGENTS produces a completed AUDIT_AGENT rubric worksheet per file.
Given explicit AGENT_*.md files, AUDIT_AGENTS produces a prioritized Issue Log.
Given explicit AGENT_*.md files, AUDIT_AGENTS produces a minimal Patch Plan.
AUDIT_AGENTS is read-only on audited files and proposes patches instead of applying them.
AUDIT_AGENTS is invoked by a Type 1 manager via an explicit brief.
RECONCILIATION and WORKING_ITEMS are typical Type 1 managers for AUDIT_AGENTS.
AUDIT_AGENTS writes only to {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/AgentAudit/.
AUDIT_AGENTS must follow the docs/rubrics/AUDIT_AGENT.md structure and evidence rules.
Every AUDIT_AGENTS finding must cite a concrete excerpt and location.
Evidence excerpts for AUDIT_AGENTS findings are limited to at most 25 words.
If the canon or rubric is missing, AUDIT_AGENTS marks checks as BLOCKER rather than guessing.
AUDIT_AGENTS must not edit audited AGENT_*.md files.
AUDIT_AGENTS proposes patches for audited files instead of applying edits.
AUDIT_AGENTS prefers the smallest change that restores conformance.
Each AUDIT_AGENTS run writes a new snapshot folder.
AUDIT_AGENTS must never overwrite prior snapshots.
AUDIT_AGENTS may overwrite _LATEST.md only as a pointer.
AUDIT_AGENTS snapshots remain immutable even when _LATEST.md is updated.
EXECUTION_ROOT is a required input with default repo-relative execution/.
FILES_TO_AUDIT is a required explicit list of AGENT_*.md paths.
TASK_BRIEF_FILE is an optional markdown brief path.
RUN_LABEL is an optional short label whose default is AGENTS.
CANON_FILE defaults to AGENT_HELPS_HUMANS.md.
If AGENT_HELPS_HUMANS.md is missing but AGENT_HELPS_HUMANS_UPDATED.md exists, AUDIT_AGENTS uses the updated file and records the substitution.
RUBRIC_FILE defaults to docs/rubrics/AUDIT_AGENT.md.
VERBOSITY accepts LOW, MED, or HIGH, with LOW as the default.
OUTPUT_FORMAT accepts RUBRIC_MARKDOWN or RUBRIC+CSV, with RUBRIC_MARKDOWN as the default.
If FILES_TO_AUDIT is missing or empty, AUDIT_AGENTS writes RUN_SUMMARY.md with RUN_STATUS FAILED_INPUTS.
If FILES_TO_AUDIT is missing or empty, AUDIT_AGENTS returns a missing-input error to the invoking manager.
AUDIT_AGENTS must not infer audit scope when FILES_TO_AUDIT is missing or empty.
AUDIT_AGENTS ensures {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/AgentAudit/ exists.
AUDIT_AGENTS ensures {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/AgentAudit/_Archive/ exists.
Each AUDIT_AGENTS run writes a new immutable snapshot folder named AUDIT_{RUN_LABEL}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{HHMM}.
The minimum AUDIT_AGENTS snapshot contents include Brief.md, RUN_SUMMARY.md, QA_Report.md, Decision_Log.md, Agent_Audit_Report.md, Agent_Audit_IssueLog.csv, and a patch plan.
RUN_SUMMARY.md records RUN_STATUS as OK, WARNINGS, or FAILED_INPUTS.
_LATEST.md is a pointer to the current AUDIT_AGENTS snapshot ID.
AUDIT_AGENTS Step 0 confirms the invocation brief is readable from a Type 1 manager.
AUDIT_AGENTS Step 0 confirms RUBRIC_FILE exists and is readable.
AUDIT_AGENTS Step 0 confirms FILES_TO_AUDIT is non-empty.
AUDIT_AGENTS Step 0 confirms CANON_FILE exists.
If the canon is missing, AUDIT_AGENTS still runs inventory and drift detection.
If the canon is missing, AUDIT_AGENTS marks canon-dependent checks as BLOCKER.
AUDIT_AGENTS records declared type, class, surface, write-scope, blocking, and outputs for each audited file.
AUDIT_AGENTS records referenced agents and contracts for each audited file.
AUDIT_AGENTS records described write behaviors and truth zones for each audited file.
AUDIT_AGENTS fills audit metadata once at run level.
AUDIT_AGENTS fills canon extraction once when canon is available.
AUDIT_AGENTS fills one rubric worksheet per audited file.
Revision version and date are informational canon check exclusions.
Normative keywords definitions are informational canon check exclusions.
Absence of Revision and Normative keywords sections is not a conformance finding for AUDIT_AGENTS.
AUDIT_AGENTS must not flag missing canon-excluded sections as WARNING, INFO, or any other severity.
Every AUDIT_AGENTS warning or failure must include an evidence excerpt and location.
Every AUDIT_AGENTS warning or failure must include a canon excerpt and location when canon is available.
Every AUDIT_AGENTS warning or failure must propose a minimal fix.
AUDIT_AGENTS Issue Log columns are ID, Severity, File(s), Type, Symptom, Evidence, CanonRequirement, and Fix.
AUDIT_AGENTS classifies BLOCKER severity as breaking core invariants.
AUDIT_AGENTS core invariants include write-scope, no-invention, and required spec outputs.
AUDIT_AGENTS classifies WARNING severity as drift or ambiguity that risks misuse.
AUDIT_AGENTS classifies INFO severity as stylistic or non-functional improvement.
AUDIT_AGENTS patch plans prefer the smallest safe edit.
When multiple fixes are possible, AUDIT_AGENTS lists options with tradeoffs instead of choosing silently.
AUDIT_AGENTS must not apply patches.
AUDIT_AGENTS Step 5 writes all artifacts into the run snapshot folder.
AUDIT_AGENTS Step 5 updates the _LATEST.md pointer.
AUDIT_AGENTS returns the snapshot path to the invoking manager.
AUDIT_AGENTS returns at most ten top issues to the invoking manager.
AUDIT_AGENTS returns blockers and a recommended next action to the invoking manager.
A valid AUDIT_AGENTS run applies the rubric to every file in FILES_TO_AUDIT.
A valid AUDIT_AGENTS run includes an evidence excerpt and location for every warning or failure.
When canon exists, a valid AUDIT_AGENTS run cites canon excerpts and locations for canon-dependent checks.
A valid AUDIT_AGENTS run produces a prioritized usable issue log.
A valid AUDIT_AGENTS run includes a patch plan as a diff or rewrite blocks.
A valid AUDIT_AGENTS run does not modify audited files.
A valid AUDIT_AGENTS run writes outputs to a new immutable snapshot folder.
The AgentAudit tool-root layout includes _Archive, _LATEST.md, and AUDIT_{RUN_LABEL}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{HHMM}/.
The AUDIT_AGENTS snapshot layout includes Brief.md, RUN_SUMMARY.md, QA_Report.md, Decision_Log.md, Agent_Audit_Report.md, Agent_Audit_IssueLog.csv, and Agent_Audit_PatchPlan.diff.
AUDIT_AGENTS audits must be traceable through evidence excerpts.
AUDIT_AGENTS audits must be low-risk by remaining read-only.
AUDIT_AGENTS audits must be actionable through an issue log and minimal patch plan.
AUDIT_AGENTS audits must be repeatable through immutable snapshots.
AUDIT_DECOMP is a Type 2 task agent that validates synchronization between a decomposition package and actual filesystem state.

AUDIT_DECOMP checks forward coverage, reverse coverage, context fidelity, artifact presence, objective mapping, scope ledger integrity, derivative-package parity, active snapshot consistency, and handoff-state consistency.
AUDIT_DECOMP audit snapshots are derivative packages that report on authoritative truth and filesystem state without replacing either one.
AUDIT_DECOMP is read-only on deliverables and the decomposition document and does not fix discrepancies.
The human has a conversation while the agent follows the AUDIT_DECOMP instruction document.
The AUDIT_DECOMP instruction version is v2.1.
The AUDIT_DECOMP v2.1 revision date is 2026-04-19.
AUDIT_DECOMP v2.1 added derivative-package parity, active snapshot completeness, handoff-state consistency, and objective-evidence integrity checks for DOMAIN_DECOMP.
Instruction files are named with AGENT_* while the agent itself is referred to by role name.
AUDIT_DECOMP has AGENT_TYPE TYPE 2.
AUDIT_DECOMP has AGENT_CLASS TASK.
AUDIT_DECOMP uses the INIT-TASK brief-driven interaction surface.
AUDIT_DECOMP write scope is limited to {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/DecompCoverage/.
AUDIT_DECOMP is never blocking.
AUDIT_DECOMP primary outputs are a coverage report, issue log CSV, coverage matrix CSV, and summary JSON.
AUDIT_DECOMP resolves conflicts by applying PROTOCOL before SPEC before STRUCTURE before RATIONALE.
If a human instruction conflicts with AUDIT_DECOMP, the agent obeys the human and records the override in Decision_Log.md.
AUDIT_DECOMP parses Ledger, Objectives, Partitions, and Production Units sections through Variant Section Binding and compares declarations against filesystem state under EXECUTION_ROOT.
AUDIT_DECOMP produces a coverage report with PASS, WARNING, and BLOCKER outcomes for 12 core checks including package-shape conformance.
AUDIT_DECOMP produces a per-deliverable coverage matrix.
AUDIT_DECOMP produces machine-readable JSON metrics.
AUDIT_DECOMP produces an actionable issue log.
AUDIT_DECOMP must never modify deliverable files, _CONTEXT.md, _STATUS.md, Dependencies.csv, or the decomposition document.
Every AUDIT_DECOMP finding must trace to a decomposition section or row and to a filesystem path or absence.
AUDIT_DECOMP marks ambiguous or missing data as UNKNOWN or INCOMPLETE and continues without inferring intent.
AUDIT_DECOMP must be deterministic: the same inputs produce the same outputs.
Each AUDIT_DECOMP run writes a new immutable snapshot folder and never overwrites prior snapshots.
AUDIT_DECOMP may overwrite _LATEST.md only as a pointer.
An AUDIT_DECOMP audit snapshot is derivative evidence for closure and handoff state, not decomposition truth.
An AUDIT_DECOMP audit snapshot must identify the authoritative inputs it evaluated.
For DOMAIN, AUDIT_DECOMP treats active decomposition-local derivatives and active _ScopeChange artifacts as auditable package state.
AUDIT_DECOMP requires EXECUTION_ROOT as an input path to the execution instance.
AUDIT_DECOMP requires DECOMPOSITION_PATH as an input path to the decomposition document.
AUDIT_DECOMP SCOPE is ALL by default or a list of package IDs or deliverable IDs.
AUDIT_DECOMP DECOMP_VARIANT is PROJECT, SOFTWARE, or DOMAIN and determines section binding, folder patterns, entity names, and ID formats.
AUDIT_DECOMP RUN_LABEL is optional and defaults to DECOMP_COV.
AUDIT_DECOMP REQUESTED_BY is optional and defaults to RECONCILIATION.
AUDIT_DECOMP PRIOR_RUN_LABEL enables comparison mode by loading prior JSON and computing deltas.
AUDIT_DECOMP EXPECTED_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT identifies the accepted upstream snapshot that the audit run is expected to evaluate and cite.
AUDIT_DECOMP EXPECTED_HANDOFF_PHASE states which closure boundary the run supports.
AUDIT_DECOMP substitutes variant-specific terms when DECOMP_VARIANT is not PROJECT.
DOMAIN_DECOMP maps the protocol term Package to Category.
DOMAIN_DECOMP maps the protocol term Deliverable to Knowledge Type.
DOMAIN_DECOMP maps the protocol term Scope Item to Handbook Unit.
DOMAIN_DECOMP maps the protocol term Scope Ledger to Domain Ledger.
DOMAIN_DECOMP maps the protocol term Artifact to Knowledge Subject.
AUDIT_DECOMP resolves protocol sections by semantic name using the Variant Section Binding table.
The Ledger semantic section binds to PROJECT_DECOMP Section 5, SOFTWARE_DECOMP Section 5, and DOMAIN_DECOMP Section 2 Domain Ledger.
The Objectives semantic section binds to dedicated sections for PROJECT_DECOMP and DOMAIN_DECOMP and to Scope Ledger ObjectiveID(s) for SOFTWARE_DECOMP.
The Partitions semantic section binds to PROJECT_DECOMP Section 7, SOFTWARE_DECOMP Section 3, and the DOMAIN_DECOMP Categories section.
The Production Units semantic section binds to PROJECT_DECOMP Section 8, SOFTWARE_DECOMP Section 4, and the DOMAIN_DECOMP Knowledge Types section.
When DECOMP_VARIANT is SOFTWARE, Check 7 resolves objectives from the Scope Ledger ObjectiveID(s) column.
PROJECT_DECOMP and SOFTWARE_DECOMP partition folders match {ROOT}/PKG-{ID}_*/.
DOMAIN_DECOMP partition folders match {ROOT}/CAT-{ID}_*/.
PROJECT_DECOMP and SOFTWARE_DECOMP production unit folders match PKG-{PID}_*/1_Working/DEL-{ID}_*/.
DOMAIN_DECOMP production unit folders match CAT-{PID}_*/1_Working/KTY-{ID}_*/.
PROJECT_DECOMP partition IDs use PKG-XXX format.
SOFTWARE_DECOMP partition IDs use PKG-XX format.
DOMAIN_DECOMP partition IDs use CAT-### format.
PROJECT_DECOMP production unit IDs use DEL-XXX-YY_{desc} format.
SOFTWARE_DECOMP production unit IDs use DEL-XX-YY format.
DOMAIN_DECOMP production unit IDs use KTY-CC-TT_{desc} format.
PROJECT_DECOMP and DOMAIN_DECOMP normalize IDs by stripping the descriptive suffix after the ID prefix.
SOFTWARE_DECOMP compares IDs directly because its IDs have no descriptive suffix.
For SOFTWARE_DECOMP, Step 5 also compares the ContextEnvelope field.
For SOFTWARE_DECOMP, Step 7 extracts objectives from the Scope Ledger ObjectiveID(s) column.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 5 also compares CanonicalSchema, IntendedUsers, and WhenUsed fields.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 6 checks Knowledge Type anticipated Knowledge Subjects instead of the standard four-document set.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 8 treats the ledger as Domain Ledger using UnitID, CategoryID, and KnowledgeTypeID(s) columns.
If DECOMPOSITION_PATH is missing, unreadable, or unparseable for required sections, AUDIT_DECOMP writes RUN_SUMMARY.md with RUN_STATUS FAILED_INPUTS and returns.
If EXECUTION_ROOT is missing or no deliverable folders are discovered, AUDIT_DECOMP writes RUN_SUMMARY.md with RUN_STATUS FAILED_INPUTS and returns.
AUDIT_DECOMP bootstraps the tool root by running tools/scaffolding/scaffold_tool_root.sh with EXECUTION_ROOT/_Reconciliation and DecompCoverage.
AUDIT_DECOMP creates a snapshot folder by running tools/scaffolding/create_snapshot_folder.sh under _Reconciliation/DecompCoverage with COV and RUN_LABEL.
AUDIT_DECOMP snapshot contents include Brief.md, RUN_SUMMARY.md, QA_Report.md, Decision_Log.md, Decomp_Coverage_Report.md, issue log CSV, coverage matrix CSV, and coverage_summary.json.
AUDIT_DECOMP updates the _LATEST.md pointer through tools/scaffolding/update_latest_pointer.sh.
Step 0 resolves EXECUTION_ROOT and DECOMPOSITION_PATH.
Step 0 parses the decomposition document into partitions, production units, objectives, and ledger entries.
Step 0 extracts each Production Unit ID, parent partition ID, name, type, responsible party, anticipated artifacts, covered atomic units, and supported objectives.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 0 maps anticipated artifacts to the Knowledge Type anticipated Knowledge Subjects.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 0 inventories active decomposition-local derivative surfaces under EXECUTION_ROOT/_Decomposition/.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 0 resolves EXECUTION_ROOT/_ScopeChange/_LATEST.md if it exists.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 0 resolves the active snapshot if _LATEST.md points to one.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 0 records whether the active snapshot contains the required artifact set.
Step 0 returns FAILED_INPUTS when parsing fails because sections are missing or table format is unrecognizable.
Step 0 discovers filesystem deliverables in scope using the Variant Folder Patterns table.
Step 0 builds a map from folder path to extracted PartitionID and ProductionUnitID.
Step 0 filters both parsed lists and discovered folders when SCOPE is a subset.
Check 1 searches for a matching folder for each Partition declared in the Partitions section.
Check 1 records PartitionID, DeclaredName, FolderFound, and FolderPath.
Check 1 emits a BLOCKER when a declared partition has no matching folder.
Check 2 searches for a matching folder for each Production Unit declared in the Production Units section.
Check 2 records ProductionUnitID, ParentPartitionID, DeclaredName, FolderFound, and FolderPath.
Check 2 emits a BLOCKER when a declared Production Unit has no matching folder under its parent partition.
Check 3 extracts the ProductionUnitID from each discovered Production Unit folder.
Check 3 verifies that each discovered Production Unit folder ID exists in the Production Units section.
Check 3 emits a WARNING when a Production Unit folder has no matching Production Units entry.
Check 3 extracts the PartitionID from each discovered Partition folder.
Check 3 verifies each discovered Partition folder ID against the Partitions section.
Check 3 emits a WARNING when a Partition folder has no matching Partitions entry.
Check 4 compares package and deliverable IDs extracted from matched folders against decomposition values.
Check 4 normalizes PROJECT_DECOMP and DOMAIN_DECOMP ID comparisons by stripping trailing labels after the ID prefix.
Check 4 compares SOFTWARE_DECOMP IDs directly because they have no descriptive suffix.
Check 4 emits a BLOCKER when the folder ID prefix does not match the decomposition ID.
Check 5 reads _CONTEXT.md for each deliverable with a matched folder.
Check 5 compares Name, Package, Type, Responsible, and Description fields against the Production Units entry.
Check 5 flags Name only when it substantially differs from the Production Units entry.
Check 5 flags Description only when semantic similarity is clearly divergent.
Check 5 compares ContextEnvelope when DECOMP_VARIANT is SOFTWARE.

Pass 1 scans Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md for epistemic label coverage.

Label coverage equals claims with explicit labels divided by total non-trivial claims identified.

Pass 2 verifies provenance for each claim with an epistemic label.
A FACT claim must have a source citation.
A FACT claim without a source citation produces a MISSING_PROVENANCE finding and K-PROV-1 violation.
An ASSUMPTION claim must be documented inline or in a referenced assumptions register.
An undocumented ASSUMPTION claim produces an UNDOCUMENTED_ASSUMPTION finding.
A PROPOSAL claim must be clearly marked as requiring a human decision.
A PROPOSAL claim that could be mistaken for decided fact produces an AMBIGUOUS_PROPOSAL finding.
A TBD claim must be actionable by identifying what is unknown and what resolution is needed.
A bare TBD placeholder without context produces a BARE_TBD finding.
Provenance completeness equals validly cited FACT claims plus documented ASSUMPTION claims divided by total FACT and ASSUMPTION claims.
Pass 3 scans all documents for explicit gaps and potential unwarranted claims.
Explicit gaps include TBD markers, location TBD provenance entries, placeholder values, TBC, TBA, N/A pending, and to be determined.
A potential unwarranted claim lacks both a source citation and a TBD marker.
A potential unwarranted claim is not labeled as ASSUMPTION or PROPOSAL.
A potential unwarranted claim appears to state specific technical content such as numeric values, material selections, standards, or design parameters.
Each potential unwarranted claim finding records the claim text and location.
Each potential unwarranted claim finding explains why the claim appears unwarranted.
Potential unwarranted claims receive WARNING severity for specific technical values and INFO severity for general statements.
Gap count equals total explicit TBD markers plus potential unwarranted claims.
Pass 4 compares key parameters, requirements, and constraints across documents within the deliverable.
Pass 4 extracts key-value assertions from each document.
Pass 4 compares values for keys that appear in multiple documents.
If key values differ across documents, Pass 4 records a CONFLICT finding.
A CONFLICT finding records the conflicting key.
A CONFLICT finding records each conflicting value with file and section evidence.
A CONFLICT finding records whether a Conflict Table entry already exists for the key.
An unrecorded conflict is flagged as UNRECORDED_CONFLICT and a K-CONFLICT-1 violation.
Conflict count equals the total parameter and value conflicts detected.
Pass 5 classifies warrant state for each claim identified in Passes 1 through 3.
UNWARRANTED applies when a claim exists without source citation and its status is TBD, PROPOSAL, or unlabeled.
CITED applies when a claim has a source citation and status FACT or ASSUMPTION.
REVIEWED applies when a claim has evidence of professional review disposition in _STATUS.md or review records.

RECONCILIATION dispatches AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE as a toolbelt agent.

If a finding impact is uncertain, the severity must be UNKNOWN and the finding must be flagged for human triage.
AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE must not guess resolution paths.
If the amendment record disagrees with filesystem state, both sides must be reported with provenance.

For SPLIT actions, Pass 1 checks that dependencies targeting the source were re-targeted or flagged.

All conforming decomposition agents run a 7-phase, gate-controlled conversational workflow.
The abstract protocol defines the invariant workflow structure.
Conforming agents extend each protocol phase with domain-specific actions, outputs, and gate language.
The agent maintains a single decomposition document as a living draft.

Phase 1 has the goal of receiving the source corpus and constraints and reflecting them back faithfully.
Phase 1 requires collecting all input material.
Phase 1 asks clarifying questions only when required to prevent structural ambiguity.
Phase 1 begins a References list identifying the inputs used.
Phase 1 outputs a title, using TBD if the title is unknown.
Phase 1 outputs a high-level intake summary.
Phase 1 outputs a References list.
Gate 1 requires human confirmation that the intake reflects the source material and context as intended.
Phase 2 has the goal of converting the source corpus into normalized atomic units that can be partitioned without losing meaning.
Phase 2 normalizes content into short, testable atomic units with one concept per unit.
Phase 2 classifies each atomic unit as IN, OUT, or TBD.
Phase 2 starts a Vocabulary Map containing canonical terms, synonyms, and notes.
Phase 2 outputs an atomic unit list with stable IDs and IN, OUT, or TBD status.
Phase 2 outputs initial objective candidates derived from the source rather than invented.
Phase 2 outputs an initial Vocabulary Map.
Gate 2 requires human confirmation that the atomic units reflect source content.
Gate 2 requires human confirmation that IN, OUT, and TBD classifications are correct.
Gate 2 requires human confirmation that vocabulary choices are acceptable.
Phase 3 has the goal of producing high-level success criteria derived from the source material.
Phase 3 derives objectives from source intent and success conditions.
Phase 3 ensures objectives are few, meaningful, and testable.
Phase 3 maps objectives to atomic units on a best-effort basis.
Phase 3 outputs an objective list with stable OBJ-NNN IDs.
Phase 3 outputs mapping notes that include unmapped objectives.
Gate 3 requires human confirmation that objectives represent success as intended.
Phase 4 has the goal of partitioning IN-scope atomic units into flat partitions.
Phase 4 proposes a flat list of partitions with stable IDs, names, scope descriptions, and inclusion or exclusion criteria.
Phase 4 assigns each IN-scope atomic unit to exactly one partition.
If an atomic unit appears to belong to multiple partitions, splitting it into smaller units is preferred when confirmed by the user.
If an atomic unit appears to belong to multiple partitions and is not split, the agent must force a decision and surface the ambiguity for human resolution.
Phase 4 outputs a partition list with IDs, names, and scope descriptions.
Phase 4 outputs atomic-unit to partition assignments in the Decomposition Ledger.
Gate 4 requires human confirmation that partitions are correct and each IN-scope unit belongs to exactly one partition.
Phase 5 has the goal of defining production units that operationalize the decomposition into bounded, actionable units.
Phase 5 defines production units within each partition.
Each production unit has a stable ID mechanically coupled to its parent partition ID.
Each production unit has a name and description.
Each production unit has a responsible party, with TBD allowed.
Each production unit has a type from the domain-specific taxonomy defined by the conforming agent.
Each production unit lists one or more anticipated artifacts, with TBD allowed.
Each production unit has best-effort objective linkage.
Each production unit has best-effort atomic unit linkage.
Phase 5 outputs the production unit list grouped by partition.
Phase 5 outputs best-effort atomic-unit to production-unit mappings in the Decomposition Ledger.
Phase 5 surfaces gaps in atomic-unit to production-unit mapping.
Gate 5 requires human confirmation that production-unit granularity, types, and responsibilities are acceptable.
Phase 6 has the goal of proving decomposition coverage and making gaps visible and trackable.
Phase 6 verifies every IN-scope atomic unit is assigned to exactly one partition.
Phase 6 verifies every IN-scope atomic unit is mapped to at least one production unit on a best-effort basis.
Phase 6 treats missing production-unit mappings as open issues.
Phase 6 verifies every production unit belongs to exactly one partition.
Phase 6 verifies objective mapping is best-effort complete.
Each objective must be supported by at least one production unit or flagged as an open issue.
Phase 6 produces a Coverage & Telemetry summary.
Phase 6 outputs the Coverage & Telemetry section.
Phase 6 outputs an Open Issues list referencing stable IDs.
Gate 6 requires human confirmation that coverage, mappings, and open issues are acceptable.
Phase 7 has the goal of producing the final decomposition document as a coherent artifact suitable for downstream work.
Phase 7 ensures the decomposition document includes all required STRUCTURE sections.
Phase 7 summarizes what changed since the last revision.
Gate 7 requires human confirmation that the decomposition is accepted as the basis for downstream work.

Domain-specific variants may add validity requirements but must not weaken the base validity requirements.

The DOMAIN decomposition workspace is a semantic system, not an execution plan.
A hypergraph represents facts that are naturally multi-party bindings.
A single ledger row can bind an atomic unit to a category, one or more Knowledge Types, and objectives.
Representing multi-party bindings as binary edges loses information or forces awkward reification.
Normalized output tables make the graph machine-checkable.

Normalized output tables keep downstream tools independent of markdown formats.
The DOMAIN graph preserves both Knowledge Subject and Knowledge Artifact layers.
Keeping subject and artifact layers distinct preserves traceability from decomposition intent to rendered documents.
Determinism and immutable snapshots preserve trust by making a run a reproducible measurement.
DRAWING_EXTRACT is a Type 1 persona agent for drawing-type-aware structured extraction from engineering drawing PDFs.
DRAWING_EXTRACT coordinates deterministic page rasterization, target-appropriate crop preparation, and TASK dispatches against a DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET tuple.
DRAWING_EXTRACT is used for selective structured extraction from drawing pages rather than full-page transcription.
The DRAWING_EXTRACT architecture splits type-agnostic core phases from target-specific repertoire hooks.
Instruction files use the AGENT_* naming convention, while agent roles use role names such as DRAWING_EXTRACT.
DRAWING_EXTRACT has AGENT_TYPE TYPE 1.
DRAWING_EXTRACT has AGENT_CLASS PERSONA.
DRAWING_EXTRACT uses chat as its interaction surface.
DRAWING_EXTRACT write scope is WORK_DIR plus a target-aware SOURCE_DIR subtree.
DRAWING_EXTRACT may block while operating.
DRAWING_EXTRACT primary outputs include target-aware combined Markdown and CSV outputs, duplicate or reconciliation CSVs, validation or merge outputs, stubs, and a work manifest.
DRAWING_EXTRACT dispatches drawing-extract-page, drawing-titleblock-page, and pandid-valve-symbol-instance via the TASK shell.
PFD, DRAWING_SET, and P_AND_ID drawing types have implemented extraction targets.

PFD supports the implemented top_equipment_header_basic extraction target.
PFD supports the implemented top_equipment_header_detailed extraction target.
P_AND_ID supports the implemented valve_count_basic extraction target.
P_AND_ID supports the implemented valve_count_detailed extraction target.
ISOMETRIC is registered as a fail-fast stub drawing type.
GA is registered as a fail-fast stub drawing type.

Any DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET combination outside the valid set rejects during Phase 0 pre-flight.

SCOPE_CHANGE classifies every change request into one or more atomic actions.
An ADD action creates a new entity or authoritative row in the decomposition.
A REMOVE action retires an existing entity non-destructively and remaps or flags downstream mappings.

A SPLIT action splits one entity into two or more successor entities with remapped references.
